design_notes: Expanded all eight topics into atomic concepts. Topic 1 contains foundational classification and measurement nodes; topic 4 is the densest because heat transfer modes, thermal properties, and blackbody radiation are all tested there. Historical contributors remain one concept per named scientist. No topic was left as a thin stub.

concepts.title: Classify thermodynamic systems
concepts.description: Identify whether a system is open, closed, or isolated by whether mass and energy cross its boundary.

concepts.title: Distinguish state and path functions
concepts.description: Classify properties such as internal energy, enthalpy, temperature, work, and heat as state functions or path functions based on path dependence.

concepts.title: Intensive vs. extensive properties
concepts.description: Determine whether a thermodynamic property is intensive or extensive and use scaling behavior to classify examples.

concepts.title: Convert temperature scales
concepts.description: Convert temperatures among Celsius, Kelvin, and Fahrenheit, and identify absolute zero on each scale.

concepts.title: Thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law
concepts.description: Apply the zeroth law to predict thermal equilibrium when systems are in contact through a diathermal boundary.

concepts.title: Temperature measurement devices
concepts.description: Compare how liquid-in-glass thermometers, thermocouples, resistance temperature detectors, and thermistors measure temperature.

concepts.title: Pressure units and manometer reading
concepts.description: Convert among pressure units and calculate gas pressure from open-tube or closed-tube manometer readings.

concepts.title: Mechanical and chemical equilibrium
concepts.description: Identify mechanical equilibrium as uniform pressure and chemical equilibrium as no net reaction or phase transfer.

topics.title: Phases, phase transitions, and heat effects

concepts.title: Phase transition names and energy direction
concepts.description: Identify melting, freezing, vaporization, condensation, sublimation, and deposition and state whether each absorbs or releases heat.

concepts.title: Read phase diagram regions and boundaries
concepts.description: Locate solid, liquid, and gas regions on a P-T phase diagram and identify melting, vaporization, and sublimation curves.

concepts.title: Triple point and critical point features
concepts.description: Interpret the triple point as the unique P-T condition for three-phase coexistence and the critical point as the end of the vapor-liquid boundary.

concepts.title: Interpret heating and cooling curves
concepts.description: Relate horizontal plateaus to phase changes and sloped segments to temperature change within a single phase on a heating or cooling curve.

concepts.title: Calculate latent heat for phase changes
concepts.description: Use q = mL to calculate the heat absorbed or released during melting, freezing, vaporization, or condensation.

concepts.title: Calculate total heat for multistep heating
concepts.description: Combine sensible heat terms q = mcΔT with latent heat terms q = mL to find the total energy for a heating or cooling problem crossing phase boundaries.

concepts.title: Vapor pressure and boiling point
concepts.description: Relate vapor pressure to boiling and explain how external pressure shifts the boiling point of a liquid.

concepts.title: Clausius–Clapeyron equation
concepts.description: Apply the Clausius–Clapeyron equation to calculate vapor pressure changes with temperature or enthalpy of vaporization.

topics.title: Ideal gas law and gas calculations

concepts.title: Ideal gas model assumptions
concepts.description: State the assumptions of the ideal gas model and judge when a real gas is most likely to behave ideally.

concepts.title: Ideal gas law calculation
concepts.description: Use PV = nRT to solve for pressure, volume, moles, or temperature of an ideal gas.

concepts.title: Molar mass from ideal gas data
concepts.description: Calculate molar mass of a gas from measured mass, volume, pressure, and temperature using the ideal gas law.

concepts.title: Gas density from the ideal gas law
concepts.description: Derive and apply d = PM/RT to calculate the density of an ideal gas or identify a gas from density.

concepts.title: Gas constant units and conversions
concepts.description: Select the appropriate value of the universal gas constant R for given pressure, volume, and energy units.

concepts.title: Standard conditions and molar volume
concepts.description: Use standard temperature and pressure (STP) to determine the molar volume of an ideal gas, commonly 22.4 L/mol.

concepts.title: Ideal gas changing-state problems
concepts.description: Apply P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2 for a fixed amount of ideal gas to find a new state after pressure, volume, or temperature changes.

concepts.title: Gas stoichiometry with the ideal gas law
concepts.description: Convert between gas volume and moles in chemical reactions using the ideal gas law and stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.title: Conduction mechanism
concepts.description: Explain conduction as energy transfer through molecular collisions or electron flow without bulk motion and identify good conductors and insulators.

concepts.title: Fourier's law and conduction calculations
concepts.description: Calculate conductive heat transfer rate through a slab using Fourier's law Q/t = kAΔT/L.

concepts.title: Convection mechanism and types
concepts.description: Distinguish natural and forced convection and describe heat transfer by bulk fluid motion.

concepts.title: Thermal radiation mechanism
concepts.description: Describe radiation as electromagnetic energy transfer that does not require a medium and explain how emissivity affects emission and absorption.

concepts.title: Stefan–Boltzmann law
concepts.description: Calculate radiated power from a surface using P = εσAT^4 and compare radiation from surfaces at different temperatures.

concepts.title: Wien's displacement law
concepts.description: Use λmax = b/T to find the peak wavelength of blackbody radiation and relate color to temperature.

concepts.title: Blackbody radiation spectrum
concepts.description: Interpret blackbody spectral curves and predict how total emitted power and peak wavelength change with temperature.

concepts.title: Heat capacity vs. specific heat
concepts.description: Distinguish heat capacity C from specific heat capacity c and convert between them using mass or moles.

concepts.title: Specific heat calculation
concepts.description: Calculate heat exchanged during a temperature change using q = mcΔT and solve for any variable.

concepts.title: Calorimetry and energy conservation
concepts.description: Use calorimetry data and conservation of energy to find specific heat, final temperature, or enthalpy change in insulated systems.

concepts.title: Isobaric process
concepts.description: Analyze processes at constant pressure and calculate work as W = PΔV.

concepts.title: Isochoric/isovolumetric process
concepts.description: Analyze processes at constant volume and explain why no pressure-volume work is done.

concepts.title: Isothermal process
concepts.description: Analyze constant-temperature processes for an ideal gas, including work calculation W = nRT ln(V2/V1).

concepts.title: Adiabatic process
concepts.description: Analyze processes with no heat transfer and use PV^γ = constant for an ideal gas.

concepts.title: P-V diagrams and work from area
concepts.description: Interpret P-V diagrams and calculate work as the area under the process curve, with sign depending on expansion or compression.

concepts.title: First law sign conventions
concepts.description: Apply ΔU = Q - W or ΔU = Q + W consistently, using the stated sign convention for heat added and work done.

concepts.title: Internal energy of an ideal gas
concepts.description: Relate internal energy change of a monatomic ideal gas to temperature change using ΔU = (3/2)nRΔT.

concepts.title: Heat engine efficiency
concepts.description: Calculate thermal efficiency from work output and heat input using η = W/Q_H and relate rejected heat to energy conservation.

concepts.title: Carnot cycle and ideal efficiency
concepts.description: Describe the Carnot cycle's four reversible steps and calculate its efficiency using η_C = 1 - T_C/T_H.

concepts.title: Refrigerator and heat pump COP
concepts.description: Calculate coefficient of performance for refrigerators and heat pumps from heat moved and work input.

concepts.title: Compare engine cycles on P-V diagrams
concepts.description: Identify and compare Otto, Diesel, and Carnot cycles by their P-V diagram shapes and idealized processes.

topics.title: Entropy, enthalpy, and the third law

concepts.title: Enthalpy definition and sign convention
concepts.description: Define enthalpy H = U + PV and interpret positive and negative enthalpy changes for processes at constant pressure.

concepts.title: Endothermic and exothermic processes
concepts.description: Classify reactions or phase changes as endothermic or exothermic from temperature change, enthalpy sign, or energy diagram.

concepts.title: Standard enthalpy of formation
concepts.description: Use standard enthalpies of formation to calculate reaction enthalpy with ΔH°rxn = ΣΔH°f(products) - ΣΔH°f(reactants).

concepts.title: Hess's law
concepts.description: Apply Hess's law to combine known thermochemical equations and determine the enthalpy change of an overall reaction.

concepts.title: Bond enthalpy calculations
concepts.description: Estimate reaction enthalpy from average bond enthalpies as energy absorbed to break bonds minus energy released forming bonds.

concepts.title: Entropy definition and microstates
concepts.description: Define entropy as a measure of energy dispersal or number of accessible microstates and predict entropy sign for simple changes.

concepts.title: Entropy change for reversible heat transfer
concepts.description: Calculate entropy change for a reversible isothermal process using ΔS = q_rev/T.

concepts.title: Second law and entropy of the universe
concepts.description: State the second law and evaluate process spontaneity using ΔS_universe = ΔS_system + ΔS_surroundings > 0.

concepts.title: Third law of thermodynamics
concepts.description: State the third law: the entropy of a perfect crystalline substance approaches zero as temperature approaches absolute zero.

concepts.title: Entropy change for phase transitions
concepts.description: Calculate entropy change during melting or vaporization using ΔS = ΔH/T at the equilibrium transition temperature.

concepts.title: Lord Kelvin and absolute temperature
concepts.description: Identify Kelvin's role in defining the absolute temperature scale and the significance of absolute zero.

concepts.title: Joseph Black and latent heat
concepts.description: Describe Black's discovery of latent heat and its role in explaining heat absorbed without temperature change during phase transitions.

concepts.title: Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat
concepts.description: Explain Joule's paddle-wheel experiment and how it established the mechanical equivalent of heat.

concepts.title: Sadi Carnot and ideal heat engine
concepts.description: Describe Carnot's idealized reversible heat engine and its implication that efficiency depends on reservoir temperatures.

concepts.title: Clausius and the second law
concepts.description: Attribute the formal statement of the second law and the introduction of entropy to Clausius.

concepts.title: Planck and blackbody radiation
concepts.description: Explain how Planck resolved the ultraviolet catastrophe by quantizing energy and introduced h in blackbody radiation theory.

concepts.title: Boltzmann's statistical entropy
concepts.description: Relate Boltzmann's equation S = k ln Ω to microstates and the statistical interpretation of entropy.

concepts.title: Maxwell's kinetic theory contributions
concepts.description: Identify Maxwell's work on molecular velocity distributions and the Maxwell relations connecting thermodynamic properties.

topics.title: Heat collection device and thermal predictions

concepts.title: Incident radiative power on collector
concepts.description: Calculate the radiative power reaching a collector area from irradiance using P_incident = I A, adjusting for orientation.

concepts.title: Energy balance for warming water
concepts.description: Equate net energy collected to water heating using Q = mcΔT and solve for energy input, mass, or temperature rise.

concepts.title: Heat collection efficiency and losses
concepts.description: Define collection efficiency as useful thermal energy delivered to water divided by incident radiative energy, and account for convective and radiative losses.

concepts.title: Predict final water temperature
concepts.description: Predict final water temperature from incident power, time, water mass, and device efficiency using an energy balance.

concepts.title: Insulation and construction constraints
concepts.description: Evaluate insulating materials, glazing, and seals for reducing conduction and convection losses within device construction rules.

concepts.title: Absorptivity and emissivity of surfaces
concepts.description: Choose collector surface properties that maximize absorption of visible/IR radiation while minimizing re-emission losses.

concepts.title: Lamp distance and intensity variation
concepts.description: Predict how irradiance on the collector changes with lamp distance, using inverse-square behavior for a point source or measured spread patterns.

concepts.title: Device testing and data analysis
concepts.description: Analyze temperature-time data from a heat collection device, identify heating rate, and compare measured final temperature to predicted value.
